prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- There’s no single tool that tells you “ChatGPT recommends X” because large language models don’t expose a public index of recommendations.  
- Best practical approach: (A) use a listings/audit tool to ensure your business appears in the authoritative sources LLMs draw from, and (B) query multiple AI assistants directly to see if they mention you.  

Recommended combo (one “best” setup)
- BrightLocal (or Yext if you want a heavier, paid enterprise solution) to check and fix local listings, citations and reviews across directories. BrightLocal is widely used by small businesses and provides an easy local-presence audit.
- Then test AI engines directly with Perplexity.ai plus ChatGPT (with browsing if available), Google Bard, Bing Chat, and Anthropic Claude to see whether they name or cite your business.

Why that combo
- LLMs and search-based chatbots rely heavily on authoritative sources (Google Business Profile, Yelp, Apple Maps, OpenStreetMap, Wikipedia/Wikidata, major review sites). BrightLocal helps you find and fix gaps across those sources so AI engines are more likely to surface you.
- Perplexity.ai gives answer outputs with sources/citations, so it’s helpful to see the provenance of recommendations. Testing directly in ChatGPT/Bard/Bing/Claude shows what users actually see.

How to test (quick steps)
1. Audit listings: run BrightLocal (or Yext) to find missing or inconsistent citations (NAP: name, address, phone). Fix inconsistencies and claim your Google Business Profile/Yelp/Apple listings.
2. Add structured data: add schema.org LocalBusiness markup to your website (name, address, phone, opening hours, geo-coordinates).
3. Get reviews: encourage authentic reviews on Google and Yelp.
4. Query AIs:
   - Perplexity.ai: “best [business type] in [city/neighborhood]” and check whether your business appears and what sources support it.
   - ChatGPT (with browsing if available): same prompt; ask “why did you recommend X?” to see what sources it used.
   - Bard, Bing Chat, Anthropic Claude: same prompt.
   - Try variations: “best [service] near me”, “top [business type] in [zip/city]”, and queries including your business name.
5. Monitor: set up BrightLocal reporting, Google Alerts, and a mention tool (Mention, Brand24) for ongoing monitoring.

Sample prompts to use
- “What are the best [pizza restaurants] in [City, Neighborhood]? List the top 5 and tell me why.”  
- “Is [Your Business Name] in [City] a highly rated [service type]? Provide sources.”  
- “Recommend an affordable [service type] near [zip code] and show citations.”

If you want, I can:
- Run a few test prompts against public models now if you give your business name and location, and report which AIs mention you and which sources they cite.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
